sources.title: Web Frontend Engineering domain manifest
claims: The registered Domain ID is engineering.web and its display name is Web Frontend Engineering.
The registered description is: Owns reusable Web frontend engineering delivery practice and evaluation.
The registered version is 0.1.0, status is draft, and owner is platform-web.

sources.title: HTML Living Standard — Semantics, structure, and APIs of HTML documents
claims: The HTML Living Standard defines the elements, semantics, structure, metadata, sections, grouping content, text-level semantics, embedded content, forms, and interactive elements used to author web documents.
HTML elements carry defined meanings and content-model constraints that frontend implementations must preserve when constructing document structure and interaction.

sources.title: HTML Living Standard — Loading web pages and origins
claims: The HTML Standard defines browser loading concepts, browsing contexts, navigation behavior, and origins.
Origins are fundamental to the web security model; actors with different origins are treated as potentially hostile and isolated to varying degrees.

sources.title: CSS Snapshot 2025
claims: CSS describes the rendering of structured documents such as HTML and XML on screen, paper, and other media.

The snapshot identifies stable CSS specifications and distinguishes them from modules with less implementation experience, so feature selection must account for specification maturity and browser adoption separately.
The stable CSS set includes media queries, conditional rules, cascading and inheritance, custom properties, box layout, color, fonts, writing modes, flexible layout, and user-interface features.

sources.title: ECMAScript Language Specification
claims: ECMA-262 defines the ECMAScript general-purpose programming language used for web scripting and application logic.
A conforming implementation provides the types, values, objects, properties, functions, syntax, and semantics described by the specification.
The living specification is the most accurate and up-to-date ECMAScript specification and includes the latest yearly snapshot plus finished proposals.

sources.title: Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) 2.2
claims: WCAG 2.2 provides recommendations for making web content more accessible across desktop, mobile, kiosk, and other devices.
WCAG 2.2 success criteria are testable, technology-independent statements organized under perceivable, operable, understandable, and robust principles.

Conformance applies to full pages, including automatically presented responsive variations, and Level AA requires satisfying all Level A and Level AA success criteria or providing a conforming alternate version.

sources.title: Developing a Keyboard Interface
claims: Custom ARIA widgets do not receive complete keyboard support from browsers automatically; authors must implement the keyboard behavior in application code.
Accessible interactive elements must be keyboard operable, with visible and predictable focus movement and established conventions for movement between and within composite components.
The guidance distinguishes keyboard focus from selection and documents focus-management strategies such as roving tabindex and aria-activedescendant.

sources.title: RFC 9110: HTTP Semantics
claims: HTTP is a stateless application-level request-response protocol with extensible semantics and self-descriptive messages.
RFC 9110 defines shared HTTP semantics across major protocol versions, including methods, status codes, representations, request and response fields, authentication, and caching-related semantics.
Frontend clients and backend services can evolve independently when they honor the uniform HTTP interface and shared message semantics.

sources.title: Content Security Policy Level 3
claims: Content Security Policy lets web developers control resources a page can fetch or execute and other security-relevant policy decisions.
CSP mitigates content-injection risk and reduces application privilege as defense in depth; it does not replace careful input validation and output encoding.
CSP supports enforced and report-only delivery through HTTP response headers, enabling monitored rollout before enforcement.

sources.title: OWASP Application Security Verification Standard
claims: OWASP ASVS provides a basis for testing technical security controls in web applications.
OWASP ASVS provides developers with security requirements for secure development and can support verification planning without substituting for organization-specific risk acceptance.

sources.title: Performance Timeline
claims: Accurate measurement of web-application performance is necessary for improving application speed.
The Performance Timeline defines primitives for accessing, instrumenting, and retrieving performance metrics across the web-application lifecycle.
Navigation Timing, Resource Timing, and User Timing contribute navigation, resource, and developer-defined measurements to the Performance Timeline.

sources.title: web-platform-tests documentation
claims: The web-platform-tests project is a cross-browser test suite for the web-platform stack.
Tests designed to run in multiple browsers give browser projects evidence about compatibility among implementations.
The project documentation covers test setup, authoring, review, and administration.

capability_hypotheses.description: Design and implement standards-based web document structure and user interfaces using HTML semantics and appropriately mature CSS capabilities across relevant presentation contexts.
Implement and evaluate browser application behavior using ECMAScript language semantics while separating language guarantees from host-environment APIs.
Engineer and verify accessible pages and interactive components against an adopted WCAG target, including keyboard operation and focus management for custom widgets.
Integrate frontend clients with web services using defined HTTP request, response, representation, status, and caching semantics.

Apply browser-origin constraints, secure frontend development requirements, and defense-in-depth controls such as monitored and enforced CSP while escalating risk acceptance to authorized security owners.
Instrument, retrieve, and evaluate browser performance measurements across navigation, resources, and application-defined work, subject to organization-approved objectives and budgets.
Create and run portable browser-facing tests that provide evidence of web-platform interoperability and rendering behavior across the organization-supported browser matrix.
